note: Marks: ours = our own run result or count (run log, post-mortem [C]); verified = a rule, decision or statement read in the named file ([V]); inferred = a projection or interpretation the source labels as such ([I], projection). No claim is unverified.

claims.text: Pilot 1 used 30 items: PREREQ 10, CROSS 10 (the 20 primary items) and 10 secondary; formats proof 15, open 10, numeric 4, MC 1.
The run made 300 Sonnet 5.5 generations (L 30, R, H and Hc 90 each) with 0 failures.
Arm G was pending; the pilot ran L, R, H and Hc, and gate 1 (all five arms) stays open until G runs.
The two judges cost USD 0.356 of the USD 1.00 cap; the cap never stopped judging.
On all 30 items (descriptive): L 28/30 (0.933), R 10/30 (0.333), H 12/30 (0.400), Hc 11/30 (0.367) fully correct.
On the 20 primary items: L 19/20, R 6/20, H 7/20, Hc 7/20; H−R b = 2, c = 1; H−Hc b = 1, c = 1.
Descriptive McNemar on 30 items: H−R b = 4, c = 2, p = 0.344; H−Hc b = 2, c = 1, p = 0.500.
99 of 391 judge calls were unparseable: valid JSON whose reason held LaTeX braces. The parser was fixed with a test, 36 generations were judged again, and MALFORMED fell to 0/165 per judge.
Before the parser fix the rates read L 0.80, R 0.27, H 0.33, Hc 0.30.
The retrieval arms abstained on 135 of 270 generations (leading sentinel), plus 1 variant that is not an abstention; L never abstained.
The registered retrieval prompt said: if the passages do not contain the answer, reply NOT_IN_MATERIAL. 25 of 30 pilot items are proof, derivation or numeric exercises.
Example prml:ex2.51 (prove trig identities from exp(iA)): both required gold passages were in H's context, and H abstained.
Abstention rate by required-gold overlap: none 62 %, part 49 %, all 38 %. Gold presence lowers abstention only weakly.
No cause is attributed: the share of the prompt and the share of retrieval in the 135 abstentions were not separated.
The placeholder router kept every edge, so H and Hc sent identical requests on 90/90 generations and identical packed lists on 30/30 items.
Gate 3 is defined on the 20 primary items; 0/20 gives an upper bound of 0.139, above 0.10, so it was not triggered and could never trigger. The log's fail (0/30, bound 0.095) used the wrong set.
R reached 0.9 B on only 12/30 items (min 2,997, median 3,547 tokens), and R, H and Hc filled alike. R already had a median of 86 candidates: the stop-packing rule, not the pool, limits fill.
H's packed list equals R's on 12/30 items: the graph changes the input on 60 % of items only.
Record defects: the rejudge manifest said generator mock, the vendored core was stale, and the judge request parameters lived outside the I2 hash.
Three candidate prompts P0, P1, P2 were hashed before tuning and chosen by an executable selector on 18 gold dev items, R and H, one generation, no judge.
Winner P2: A_present P0 5/12, P1 5/24, P2 1/12; marker validity P2 32/33.

Scope line: arms answer under a passage-restricted prompt; the model answers most items without retrieval (pilot p_L 0.93), so C2 tests which retrieval gives a passage-restricted tutor more judged-correct answers.
A correctness-plus-gold-citation proxy is added as a secondary McNemar, labelled unadjusted; it never enters the C2 decision.
T10 is replaced: R's used tokens not below H's and Hc's, and R's median at least 0.80 B. Stop packing (rule 10) is kept; first-fit is withdrawn.
Gate 3 is restated on all 30 items: triggered if s = 0/30 (1/30 gives 0.149) or no primary item differs; it is evaluated once, on pilot 2 only.
Dev set v2: 18 answerable candidates and 2 cluster siblings move to dev, 45 bank items; main excludes 99 ids in 84 clusters.
I3 hashes the judge request parameters, the selected prompt, the router, k_graph, the new T10 and a committed core.
Pilot 2 is an exposed development rerun: same 30 items, all five arms, R, H, Hc × 3, L × 3, G × 1; its estimates are descriptive.
R's winner: depth 30, rerank_top 10 (gold recall 89/216 = 0.412). H: all 9 configurations tie at 77/216; the pre-stated tie rule picks s7-b/2, k_graph 10.
In pilot 1 as run, 29/30 graph lists were all hop 0: only 1 of 30 held a deeper-hop passage (lfd-problem-2.1: 3 hop-0, 17 hop-1).
Under I3 (rule 7, k_graph 10) H and Hc retrieval would be identical on 30/30 items, so 0/30 lists would differ. This assumes the same seeds; it is a projection, not an observation.

Balanced rank: each hop present gets ⌈slots left / hops left⌉ slots by CE score (4/3/3 at 10); free slots are backfilled in rule-7 order without removing a deeper pick; the set is returned in (hop, −CE, id) order.
Rule 8 is read as an equal cap (want = k_graph), not an equal length; shortages are disclosed per item and arm.
The balanced rule needed 181,630 new (question, passage) pairs. All 25 scoring kernels matched the 200-key overlap bit for bit, so S1 was kept; 197,073 scores were merged at 100 % coverage.
H re-tuned under D: three-way tie at k_graph 30 (77/216), decided by the tie rule: s7-b/2, k_graph 30.
I4 (config 7cae3a31…): s7-b/2, k_graph 30, depth 30, rerank_top 10, hop-balanced/1; I3 marked superseded.

Arm G: 8/8 extraction shards done; the first full build stopped at Kaggle's 12 h limit at merge stage 289 of 394; a clean staged rebuild is running. G's index is one recorded instance, not bit-reproducible.
44 of 50 sampled pairs reach the 512-token cap of the cross-encoder; RRF can let R's list take over the context, and this dominance is reported per item.
Under the selected table, 15 of 30 pilot questions take the default row, where H and Hc allow the same edges.
Fourteen rules close the channels through which labels could reach Hc in our pipeline; topology, node text and graph construction stay open.
Tagger agreement: kappa 0.33 on the exact stratum, 0.20 on primary membership (95 % interval 0.15 to 0.26).
Unchanged by the fixes: S_G, S_P, gold, strata, bank and reference answers. I2 is replaced by I3.
I0 (config 6127e269…) refers to the first graph S_G 6e1d2540, with placeholder router and k_graph; kept as the baseline.
A blinded audit found 11 of 50 PREREQUISITE_OF edges wrong, so a judge pass made a new graph and a new S_G.
I1 (config f8a772f0…) on S_G 5c66b0d2; Sonnet 5.5 is the only answer model.
I2 (config bb5615ec…) on the final S_G 7f28a3a3 after the restore; pilot 1 ran under I2.
I3 (config 1bd69f9b…) is superseded; I4 governs the second pilot and the main run.
L answers without retrieval under its own prompt and is generated three times from pilot 2 on; G answers once. In pilot 1, L ran once.
An equal cap does not mean equal tokens or equal passage counts; used tokens and list lengths are reported per item and arm.
Addendum C amends the registration; it does not preserve it. Each replaced rule is labelled a replacement in ch3 and ch4.
Judge agreement: same verdict 153/165, kappa 0.77; MC 8/8 agree with exact match.
The first pilot was an implementation failure that changed the design, not evidence about C2.
